pointers.sentence: Two more give, for a date, the first day of its period and of the next (`django/views/generic/dates.py:MonthMixin`).
And `DateMixin.uses_datetime_field` reports whether the field is a `models.DateTimeField`, which decides how the lookups on the field are written (`django/views/generic/dates.py:DateMixin`).
The three go into `get_context_data`, and the context into `render_to_response` (`django/views/generic/dates.py:BaseDateListView`).
And the list is ordered by the date field, newest first, unless the view sets an `ordering` (`django/views/generic/dates.py:BaseDateListView.get_ordering`).

That function builds one string from the values and another from the formats, joined by a delimiter, and has `strptime` parse the first by the second (`django/views/generic/dates.py:_date_from_string`).

Every period of the date views is defined so, as start date <= item date < next start date (`django/views/generic/dates.py:BaseMonthArchiveView.get_dated_items`, `django/views/generic/dates.py:MonthMixin._get_next_month`).

Every period of the date views is defined so, as start date <= item date < next start date (`django/views/generic/dates.py:BaseMonthArchiveView.get_dated_items`, `django/views/generic/dates.py:MonthMixin._get_next_month`).

`DateMixin.uses_datetime_field` is worked out at the first boundary and kept for the rest of the request (`django/views/generic/dates.py:DateMixin.uses_datetime_field`), and each boundary comes back as midnight with its offset:

The boundaries are midnight in the current time zone so that what a page lists agrees with the period its URL names: an article published late on 31 March in the current time zone belongs to March whatever its timestamp is in UTC ([Time zones](../i18n/time-zones.md)) (`django/views/generic/dates.py:DateMixin._make_date_lookup_arg`).

`BaseDateListView.get_dated_queryset` applies the interval to the view's queryset and, with the defaults, adds one condition the URL does not give, an upper bound at the present moment, and then tests whether anything is left (`django/views/generic/dates.py:BaseDateListView.get_dated_queryset`).
The list is a second query, a `SELECT DISTINCT` over the same interval, with each date cut to its day (`django/views/generic/dates.py:BaseDateListView.get_date_list`):
`MonthMixin.get_next_month` and `get_previous_month` hand the question to `_get_next_prev`, which is written never to offer such a link (`django/views/generic/dates.py:_get_next_prev`).

For April, the month the clock is in, the search for a next month asks for an article dated at or after 1 May and at or before the present moment, which none can be: `_get_next_prev` returns `None`, and April's page offers no next month, though the Gazette has an article in May (`django/views/generic/dates.py:_get_next_prev`).
